title: Evangelism
definition: Evangelism is the faithful sharing of the Gospel of Jesus Christ with those who need salvation.
summary: Evangelism is the faithful sharing of the Gospel of Jesus Christ with those who need salvation.
christFocus: Jesus seeks and saves the lost, sends His people as witnesses, and empowers Gospel proclamation through the Holy Spirit.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Evangelism is not pressuring people into religion or promoting a ministry brand. It is bearing witness to Jesus Christ—the crucified and risen Savior who calls sinners to repentance and faith.

Scripture gives both the message and the manner of evangelism. Believers speak truth with love, humility, clarity, courage, and dependence on the Holy Spirit.

Every believer can bear witness. Some preach publicly, some teach, some share personally, some invite, some testify, some pray and serve. The power is in the Gospel, not the personality of the messenger.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many Christians feel too unqualified, afraid, or broken to share Christ. Evangelism reminds them that witnesses do not save anyone; they point to the Savior who does.

This doctrine also keeps outreach from becoming vague encouragement. People need hope, but the deepest hope is Jesus Himself.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pray for someone who needs Christ and look for a faithful opportunity to share the Gospel. Speak clearly about Jesus, depend on the Spirit, and trust God with the results.
